title: exec-staff-meeting-prep-notes-2026-03-17
summary: Prep notes for weekly exec staff meeting. Focus on Q2 priorities alignment, Dedicated capacity rollout risks, and hiring runway ask.
content:
Attendees: CTO (Samir), COO (Elena), Head Product (Carlos), Head SRE (Maya), Head Applied ML (Rina), Head Sales (Jordan)

Purpose: quick alignment on top risks and asks we need to bring to board/exec sponsors this week. Keep to 30m.

Agenda:
- 5m: Quick updates (ops/issues that block customers)
- 10m: Q2 priorities check (dedicated, private, optimize) - confirm tradeoffs and dependencies
- 8m: Dedicated rollout risks + mitigation ask (capacity, SLA language, partner onboarding)
- 5m: Hiring & runway ask + decision on extra contractor budget
- 2m: AOB / decisions loop closure

Background/context:
- Dedicated GA is targeted mid-Q2; internal QA is ~85% green but we have two outstanding scaling issues on multi-tenant control plane under burst.
- Several enterprise prospects are asking for private deployment timelines and KMS integration details; sales requests a firm date or a phased commitment.
- Hiring: current runway assumes headcount plan frozen; recruiting slower than expected for infra SRE and platform-engineering senior ICs.

Key metrics to call out (have slides ready):
- Current Dedicated perf tests: p95 latency 180ms (target 150ms) at 75% utilization; tail behavior spikes at high burst.
- Customer beta feedback NPS: 7.8 (target >=8.5) — main issues: documentation gaps, onboarding speed.
- Hiring funnel: 4 active offers, 9 candidates in final loop, time-to-offer 45 days (goal 30).
- Cash/runway: runway 14 months at current burn; hiring freeze would extend to 18 months.

Talking points / asks for execs:
- Decision: approve an additional $200k contractor budget to accelerate two infra hires and reduce time-to-production for Dedicated (yes/no).
- Ask: approve a temporary SLA relaxation for early Dedicated customers (explicit warning in contract) while we complete scaling fixes; propose canary customers only for first 6 weeks.
- Ask: authorize an external SRE consultant (2 months) to triage burst behavior and advisor for control plane autoscaling.
- Decision: commit to phased Private deployment schedule to provide sales with dates (Phase 1: KMS + VPC by end of Q2, Phase 2: on-prem alpha in early Q3).

Risks / mitigations (short):
- Risk: control plane scaling bug causes degraded performance for Dedicated customers on burst -> Mitigation: reduce per-pool max burst, enable circuit-breaker routing to hosted variants, engage consultant.
- Risk: sales over-promises Private GA -> Mitigation: publish phased dates, add explicit gating criteria, align CSM on messaging.
- Risk: hiring delays -> Mitigation: reallocate budget to contractors for critical path, reduce non-critical feature work.

Notes for the meeting flow:
- Start with the one-slide state (metrics above) + 1 slide per ask (contractor budget, SLA relax, phased private dates).
- Keep discussion focused on decisions; capture unresolved items as action items.

Action items (owner / due):
- "Draft contractor budget justification and scope for infra contractors" (Maya) - due 2026-03-19
- "Prepare SLA relaxation language + risk disclosure for legal review" (Elena) - due 2026-03-18
- "Run targeted stress test for control plane burst scenarios and share log samples" (Head SRE - Rina) - due 2026-03-18
- "Sales: freeze external customer commitments on Private GA dates until exec decision" (Jordan) - due 2026-03-17
- "Create phased Private deployment timeline and gate criteria doc" (Carlos) - due 2026-03-20
- "Eng: scope consultant statement of work + vendor shortlist" (Samir) - due 2026-03-18

Follow-up / intended outcomes:
- Clear binary decisions on contractor spend and SLA relaxation so legal/finance can operate over the week.
- A short public exec note to sales + CSM summarizing agreed dates and gating (if decisions made).
- If contractor approved, hire kickoff and consultant engagement + daily standup with SRE for 2 weeks.

Open questions to surface:
- Do we accept a short-term SLA caveat for early Dedicated customers?
- Is $200k the right number or do we need to budget more for faster ramp?
- Which customers (if any) do we let into Phase 1 Private?

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Bring 2 example customer MSA language snippets to meeting.
- Have cost delta slide for contractor vs delayed feature revenue.
- If exec pushes back, propose 4-week postponement of public Dedicated GA instead of contractors (tradeoff to surface).

End of prep notes.
